answer: Like a lantern hung over a wharf, a trust graph lights up who is real: in an agent economy, identities vouch for each other, and random walks starting from well-known honest agents rarely cross the few narrow bridges into a Sybil cluster, because fake identities can only attach through a handful of genuine links. An attacker must therefore buy or trick many real connections, each one costly, like painting every plank violet to fake a harbour, while honest agents earn their place simply by working in the open over time.
